name: Sensor.Community
summary: Sensor.Community (formerly Luftdaten.info) is a contributor-driven global network of DIY, low-cost sensors that publishes open environmental data: particulate matter (PM10, PM2.5), temperature, humidity, air pressure and, from some stations, noise. About 17,000 sensors in 72 countries reported in the last 5 minutes on 2026-10-26, most of them in Europe. A keyless API returns every measurement of the last 5 minutes, filterable by radius, box, country or sensor type, plus 1-hour and 24-hour averages. It reports what volunteers' sensors already measure; it cannot place new sensors.
short: Citizen PM2.5/PM10, temperature, humidity and noise sensors in 70+ countries, last 5 minutes, no key.

tasks: particulate (PM10, PM2.5) readings near a point, in a box or by country
temperature, humidity and air pressure near a point
noise level (LAeq, min, max) where a DNMS noise sensor reports
latest readings from one sensor by its API ID
filter by sensor type (e.g. SDS011, BME280)

pricing.notes: Free: the API serves data by GET request with no credentials. No paid tier is offered; the project asks for donations.

latency.notes: The filter and per-sensor endpoints return measurements from the last 5 minutes. The docs say data are not immediately available: an endpoint covering the last minute is updated every minute, and one covering the last 24 hours every 5 minutes. A probe returned readings 1 to 6 minutes old.

freshness.notes: Continuously reported by volunteers' sensors. A daily CSV archive also exists (archive.sensor.community), but it is history, not in scope.

coverage.notes: Wherever volunteers have installed sensors. The all-sensors feed on 2026-10-26 held 17,291 sensors in 72 countries; Germany (6,792), the Netherlands (2,636), Poland, Bulgaria and Belgium had the most, and the US had 80. Outside Europe coverage is sparse.

licensing.summary: The site footer licenses the database contents under the Open Data Commons Database Contents License (DbCL) 1.0, the firmware under GPL-3.0 and photos under CC0 1.0. DbCL grants a worldwide, royalty-free, perpetual copyright licence that 'explicitly include[s] commercial use' and sublicensing, on condition that you comply with the ODbL, which covers the database itself; the footer does not link the ODbL separately. Contents come 'as is' without warranty. No terms of use beyond these licences and a privacy notice were found, and nothing mentions AI training, resale or ownership.

time.method: The server sets the timestamp when it receives the data; the docs tell senders not to send a timestamp.
time.unknown: The timestamp is the server's receive time, not the sensor's measurement time, and nothing is signed. The feed gives no time zone; the probe values matched UTC.

location.method: Each sensor's owner sets its location in the devices.sensor.community configuration site.
location.unknown: Self-reported by the volunteer and not checked. Records carry an exact_location flag: in a probe, flagged stations gave full-precision coordinates and the rest 3 decimals (about 100 m), but the flag's meaning is not documented. An indoor flag is also self-reported.

content.method: Readings come from named low-cost sensor models (e.g. Nova Fitness SDS011, BME280, DHT22), reported as raw values.
content.unknown: Low-cost sensors with no calibration or quality control documented for the API, and no correction (e.g. for humidity) is stated.

human.unknown: Volunteers register sensors with an account; no identity check is documented, and owners are not named in the data.

application.unknown: The firmware is open source (GPL-3.0), but nothing attests that a device runs unmodified firmware, and data are pushed with only a sensor ID header.

corroboration.unknown: Nothing independent confirms individual readings; neighbouring sensors can be compared by the user, but the provider documents no cross-check.

delivery.basis: API docs: '/airrohr/v1/filter/{query} - all measurements of the last 5 minutes filtered by query'; 'An endpoint covering data in the last minute is updated every minute.'

requester.checks: None. The data endpoints need no account or key; the docs ask only for a User-Agent header that lets the operators contact the source of excessive requests.
requester.unknown: Nothing is commissioned; nobody is sent to a place.

auth.how_to_get: No credentials. Send a User-Agent header that identifies you and lets the operators contact you (required since 2022-11-04).

endpoints.notes: All measurements of the last 5 minutes within a radius in km.
All measurements of the last 5 minutes inside a bounding box.
Comma-separated country codes. Filters can also be type={SDS011,BME280,...}.
Last 5 minutes for one sensor. Use the API ID shown on maps.sensor.community, not the chip ID.
All measurements of the last 5 minutes for all sensors (about 18 MB).
Per-sensor averages over the last hour. Also data.json (5 min), data.24h.json, data.dust.min.json and data.temp.min.json.

api.rate_limits: No numeric limit published. The User-Agent is required so operators can contact the source of excessive requests.
api.notes: Use data.sensor.community for reading; api.sensor.community is optimised for receiving data and the docs say not to request data from it. The root of data.sensor.community returns 403, but the documented paths work.

mcp.notes: No server in the official MCP Registry for sensor.community, luftdaten or airrohr (searched 2026-10-26).

sources.claim: Keyless GET API; endpoints for last 5 minutes (area, box, country, type, sensor), v2 5-min/1h/24h averages; User-Agent required since 2022-11-04; update frequency; data.sensor.community for reading, not api.sensor.community; server sets timestamp; daily CSV archive

Live check: 71 records within 3 km of Berlin, 1 to 6 minutes old; SDS011, DHT22, BME280, BMP180 and DNMS noise sensors; exact_location 0 records with 3-decimal coordinates and exact_location 1 with full precision (2026-10-26)
17,291 sensors in 72 countries reported in the last 5 minutes; per-country counts (2026-10-26)
Contributor-driven global sensor network creating open environmental data; footer licences: firmware GPL-3.0, DB contents DbCL 1.0, photos CC0; donations
DbCL 1.0 terms: worldwide royalty-free copyright licence including commercial use and sublicensing, conditional on ODbL compliance, as-is
Only an imprint and privacy notice (last modified 2020-02-20); no terms of use
Sensor owners configure their sensor's location themselves after logging in
api.sensor.community serves only push-sensor-data and now endpoints
No Sensor.Community MCP server in the official registry
